CHECKPOINT / THREE FILESExternal PGN + dictionary required

Atlas45 · checked plans with the same canonical definitions. This HTML contains the interface, verifier and acceptance hashes only. Load the external PGN and dictionary. No embedded copies or substitutions.

Both external files are mandatory. The selected dictionary defines the grammar, predicates, certificates and plan contract. Wrong or mixed versions are rejected without replacing either file.

An explicitly selected ZIP supplies its PGN and dictionary. Matching workspace notes can be restored, but no files are substituted or relabeled.



What the integrity boundary does
Executable modules and the core specification are checked by hashes. The editor can author theorem data and derives its variable tree, registry, and PGN dictionary stamps. The independent Worker validates source, entry, graph, and ending obligations before accepting a change. The PGN is the concrete puzzle record.
The JSON contains definitions only. Every concrete defense is stored as ordinary PGN movetext with readable NODE anchors. Positions, piece identities, classes, and usage indexes are rebuilt in memory from that text. Nothing missing from the PGN is recovered from the dictionary.
Checksums are tamper-evidence against a known checkpoint, not a digital signature or protection against rewriting the verifier itself.

Use +/− to expand or collapse a node. Initially only the mainline is expanded. Folded rows are a display convenience: exports always contain the entire authoritative PGN. The blue box shows the actual selected variation. Click a move to jump to its board. Click ENTRY or a predicate to see its before-move bindings. Click PRE to return to the earlier same-piece observation. Defense-class member buttons open the actual branches recorded in the PGN. Structural NODE anchors can be shown with the metadata toggle. Line numbers are only a reading aid and never enter the PGN.

 








Frozen Lichess reference · 2026-09-10. 500 numbered examples. PGN semantics: accepted END/CERT conjunctions and acyclic JOINs; OPEN remains unresolved. No REASON annotation or alternative terminal layer. The complete specification is loaded from dictionary-spec.json and used by every PGN export. This HTML has no built-in corpus or dictionary fallback. Three-ply mate-threat trees, persistent attack/alignment preconditions, and a fixed theorem/composition/JOIN registry. Castling is a move type, not a theorem. No new engine analyses.
